nodes.text: We call a sequence of integers $0\leq a_1<\cdots <a_k$ admissible if it is missing at least one congruence class modulo every prime $p$. Let $A(k)=\min a_k$. Estimate $A(k)$ - in particular, is it true that\[A(k)\sim k\log k?\]Estimate\[B(k)=\min \frac{a_1+\cdots+a_k}{k}.\]

#1204 : [Er80,p.108] number theory Erdős [Er80] attributes this problem to Elliott. The bounds are misstated in [Er80] , but it is known that\[(1/2+o(1))k\log k \leq A(k)\leq (1+o(1))k\log k.\]The upper bound Erdős attributes to Davenport, and follows simply by taking the $k$ smallest primes $>k$. The lower order terms have been improved by Hensley and Richard [HeRi73] (see Section 10 of [Po14c] for more details). The lower bound is originally due to Elliott [El65] , but was rediscovered by the Polymath project on bounded gaps between primes (see [Po14c] ). An upper bound of $\pi(x+y)\leq \pi(x)+(1+o(1))\pi(y)$ (see [855] ) together with the prime tuples conjecture would imply $A(k)\geq (1+o(1))k\log k$. It is trivial that $B(k)<A(k)$. Taking the first $k$ primes which are $>k$ implies\[B(k)\leq (1/2+o(1))k\log k,\]and since $a_j\geq A(j)$ we have $B(k) \geq \frac{1}{k}\sum_{1\leq j\leq k}A(j)$, whence if $A(k)\geq (c-o(1))k\log k$ we have $B(k) \geq (c/2-o(1))k\log k$, and so it is likely that\[B(k)\sim(1/2+o(1))k\log k.\]In [Er80] Erdős also asks about the behaviour of $a_k$ where $a_1<a_2<\cdots$ is the greedy admissible sequence (i.e. $a_1=0$ and $a_{i+1}$ is the smallest integer $>a_{i-1}$ such that $a_1,\ldots,a_i$ is admissible).
